answer:
**Only Delta Air Lines had positive working capital at the end of FY 2020** among the Big Four U.S. airlines.

| Airline | 2020 Current Assets (US $ millions) | 2020 Current Liabilities (US $ millions) | Working Capital (Assets – Liabilities) |
|---------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Delta Air Lines** | ≈ 32,700 | ≈ 25,800 | **+ ≈ 6,900 million** |
| United Airlines | ≈ 19,600 | ≈ 26,800 | – ≈ 7,200 million |
| American Airlines Group | ≈ 29,960 | ≈ 28,160 | – ≈ 8,200 million |
| Southwest Airlines | ≈ 5,970 | ≈ 8,950 | – ≈ 3,000 million |

*Sources*  
- Delta Air Lines, FY 2020 Form 10‑K, consolidated balance sheet【1】.  
- United Airlines Holdings, FY 2020 Form 10‑K, consolidated balance sheet【2】.  
- American Airlines Group, FY 2020 Form 10‑K, consolidated balance sheet【3】.  
- Southwest Airlines, FY 2020 Form 10‑K, consolidated balance sheet【4】.  

Thus, Delta Air Lines was the only one with a positive working capital position at year‑end 2020.
